claims.sentence: T-tests and age-adjusted regression analyses were used to compare participants who met DSM-5 diagnostic criteria for chronic insomnia disorder and sleep apnea (COMISA) vs OSA alone.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Results</jats:title> <jats:p>In 128 veterans (Mage=64.6 years, 89% male, 19.5% Hispanic, 35.9% Black, 9.4% American Indian/Alaska Native, mean comorbidity index=5.5, BMI=32.2) with no/limited PAP use, COMISA (n=77, mean ISI=13.3) was associated with worse PSQI [7.8 vs 10.9], ESS [7.6 vs 9.6] and sleep-related function (FOSQ-10 15.6 vs 14.1) vs OSA alone (n=51, mean ISI=8.9) (all P<.05) despite no differences in AHI.</jats:p> </jats:sec> <jats:sec> <jats:title>Conclusion</jats:title> <jats:p>Among veterans with moderate-to-severe OSA and no/limited current PAP use, those with comorbid insomnia disorder (COMISA) have worse sleep quality, more daytime sleepiness and worse sleep-related function.
